# Preterite Tense — Irregular Verbs

## Overview
The most common Spanish verbs are irregular in the preterite. Since storytelling requires verbs like ir (go), hacer (do/make), tener (have), and estar (be), irregular preterites are unavoidable from the very first past-tense conversation. The good news: irregular preterites fall into predictable groups with shared stems and a unique set of endings (no accent marks).

## When to Teach
- Phase: B
- Prerequisites: B-01-preterite-regular
- L1 interference to preempt: none (forms don't have an English parallel to interfere)

## The Pattern

Irregular preterite verbs use **changed stems** combined with a **special set of endings** different from regular preterites. The key rule: **irregular preterite endings have NO accent marks** on yo or él/ella/usted.

### Irregular Preterite Endings (Shared by All Groups)

| Person | Ending |
|--------|--------|
| yo | **-e** (no accent) |
| tú | **-iste** |
| él / ella / usted | **-o** (no accent) |
| nosotros/as | **-imos** |
| vosotros/as | **-isteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **-ieron** (except J-stem: **-eron**) |

> **Critical difference from regular preterite:** Regular: hablé, habló (accented). Irregular: tuve, tuvo (NO accent). Adding accents to irregular forms is one of the most common errors.

### Group 1: U-Stem Verbs

These verbs change their stem to include a "u":

| Infinitive | Stem | Yo | Él/Ella |
|-----------|------|-----|---------|
| tener (have) | tuv- | **tuve** | **tuvo** |
| estar (be) | estuv- | **estuve** | **estuvo** |
| poder (be able) | pud- | **pude** | **pudo** |
| poner (put) | pus- | **puse** | **puso** |
| saber (know) | sup- | **supe** | **supo** |
| haber (there be) | hub- | **hube** | **hubo** |
| andar (walk) | anduv- | **anduve** | **anduvo** |

Full example with tener: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron.

### Group 2: I-Stem Verbs

These verbs change their stem to include an "i":

| Infinitive | Stem | Yo | Él/Ella |
|-----------|------|-----|---------|
| hacer (do/make) | hic- | **hice** | **hizo** |
| querer (want) | quis- | **quise** | **quiso** |
| venir (come) | vin- | **vine** | **vino** |

> **Spelling note:** Hacer changes c to z in the 3rd singular (hizo, not hico) to preserve the /s/ sound before -o.

### Group 3: J-Stem Verbs

These verbs have stems ending in "j". The 3rd plural drops the "i" in -ieron, becoming **-eron**:

| Infinitive | Stem | Yo | Él/Ella | Ellos |
|-----------|------|-----|---------|-------|
| traer (bring) | traj- | **traje** | **trajo** | **trajeron** |
| decir (say) | dij- | **dije** | **dijo** | **dijeron** |
| producir (produce) | produj- | **produje** | **produjo** | **produjeron** |

> **Key:** All -ducir verbs (conducir, traducir, reducir) follow the producir pattern: conduje, traduje, reduje. The 3rd plural is always -eron, NOT -ieron.

Note: decir is sometimes listed with I-stem verbs because of the vowel change (e to i), but its J-stem in the preterite is the defining feature.

### Group 4: Completely Irregular

**Ir and ser** share identical preterite forms (context determines meaning):

| Person | Ir / Ser |
|--------|----------|
| yo | **fui** |
| tú | **fuiste** |
| él / ella / usted | **fue** |
| nosotros/as | **fuimos** |
| vosotros/as | **fuisteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **fueron** |

- Fui al mercado. (I went to the market.) -- ir
- Fue una buena película. (It was a good movie.) -- ser

**Dar** uses -er/-ir regular endings on an irregular stem (short, no accents):

| Person | Dar |
|--------|-----|
| yo | **di** |
| tú | **diste** |
| él / ella / usted | **dio** |
| nosotros/as | **dimos** |
| vosotros/as | **disteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **dieron** |

### Group 5: Spelling Changes (Yo Form Only)

These verbs are regular in all forms EXCEPT the yo form, where a spelling change preserves the original pronunciation:

| Pattern | Example | Yo Form | Why |
|---------|---------|---------|-----|
| -car → -qué | buscar (search) | **busqué** | c → qu before e to keep /k/ sound |
| -gar → -gué | llegar (arrive) | **llegué** | g → gu before e to keep /g/ sound |
| -zar → -cé | empezar (begin) | **empecé** | z → c before e (Spanish spelling rule) |

All other forms are regular: buscaste, buscó, buscamos, buscasteis, buscaron.

## Examples in Context

1. Ayer **fui** al supermercado y **compré** frutas. (Yesterday I went to the supermarket and bought fruit.)
2. **Hizo** mucho calor la semana pasada. (It was very hot last week.)
3. No **pudimos** encontrar el restaurante. (We couldn't find the restaurant.)
4. ¿**Tuviste** que trabajar el sábado? (Did you have to work on Saturday?)
5. Mi amigo me **dijo** que la película **fue** buena. (My friend told me the movie was good.)
6. **Vinieron** a las ocho y **trajeron** comida. (They came at eight and brought food.)
7. **Estuve** enfermo toda la semana. (I was sick all week.)
8. **Puse** las llaves en la mesa, pero no las **encontré**. (I put the keys on the table, but I didn't find them.)
9. **Supe** la verdad cuando **hablé** con ella. (I found out the truth when I spoke with her.)
10. **Llegué** tarde porque no **pude** encontrar estacionamiento. (I arrived late because I couldn't find parking.)

## L1 Interference

**English habit:** English irregular past tenses are memorized one by one (go/went, do/did, have/had) with no grouping pattern. Learners may try to memorize each Spanish irregular individually.

**Spanish reality:** Irregular preterites cluster into predictable groups. Learn the stem, apply the shared endings. This is more systematic than English.

**Preemption script:** "Unlike English, where each irregular past is totally different (go/went, eat/ate, see/saw), Spanish irregular preterites follow GROUP patterns. If you learn the stem 'tuv-' for tener, you already know the pattern for estar (estuv-), poder (pud-), and poner (pus-). Same endings for all of them."

## Common Errors

1. **Adding accents to irregular forms:** Writing "tuvé" or "tuvó" instead of tuve, tuvo. The irregular endings are unstressed -- this is the opposite of regular preterites. -- overgeneralization from regular preterite pattern.
2. **Regularizing irregular stems:** Producing "hací" instead of hice, or "tení" instead of tuve. -- developmental. The irregular stem must replace the infinitive stem entirely.
3. **Ir/ser confusion in preterite:** "Fue al mercado" -- did someone go, or was it at the market? -- developmental. Context always resolves it, but learners need reassurance that ambiguity is rare.
4. **J-stem 3rd plural error:** "Dijieron" instead of dijeron, "trajieron" instead of trajeron. -- overgeneralization. The -ieron ending loses its "i" after "j".
5. **Spelling change overapplication:** Applying -car/-gar/-zar changes to ALL forms instead of just yo. -- overgeneralization. Only the yo form changes because only -é triggers the spelling adjustment.

## Teaching Sequence

### Stage 1: Noticing
Show a short story about yesterday using 6 high-frequency irregular preterites. Ask: "These are all past tense, but they look different from the regular preterites we learned. Can you spot any patterns?"
- **Fui** al centro con mi amiga. **Hicimos** muchas cosas. Primero **tuvimos** que buscar estacionamiento. Después **anduvimos** por las calles. Mi amiga **quiso** comprar ropa, pero no **pudo** encontrar su talla.

Then reveal the U-stem group: "Look at tuve, pude, anduve -- what do they share?"

### Stage 2: Controlled Practice
Stem-matching drill: given the infinitive, learner supplies the irregular stem. Then full conjugation: given stem + subject, learner produces the form. Group by stem type. Most frequent first: ir/ser (fui), hacer (hice), tener (tuve), estar (estuve). Add remaining groups gradually over multiple sessions.

### Stage 3: Guided Production
Prompt: "Tell me about something interesting that happened to you recently. Try to use at least 3 of these verbs: ir, hacer, tener, poder, decir, traer, venir." Provide the stem as a hint if needed (e.g., "Remember: hacer becomes hic-").

### Stage 4: Communicative Practice
Prompt: "Tell me the story of a trip or vacation. Where did you go? What did you do? What happened?" This naturally requires a mix of ir (fui a...), hacer (hicimos...), tener (tuvimos que...), poder (pudimos/no pudimos...), and regular preterites for a complete narrative.

## Dialect Notes
**Vosotros** irregular forms (tuvisteis, hicisteis, fuisteis) follow the same pattern -- the irregular stem + -isteis. Latin American Spanish skips these entirely, using ustedes + 3rd plural (tuvieron, hicieron, fueron).

**Voseo:** Preterite vos forms are identical to tú forms (tuviste, hiciste, fuiste). No vos-specific irregularity.

See `curriculum/dialect-notes.yaml` for vocabulary differences by region.

## Signs of Acquisition
- **Scaffolded:** Given an infinitive and subject, produces the correct irregular preterite form. Can identify stem groups (U-stem, I-stem, J-stem) and apply endings without accent marks.
- **Unscaffolded:** Uses high-frequency irregular preterites (fui, hice, tuve, estuve, dijo) naturally in narration without pausing to recall stems. Mixes irregular and regular preterites in the same story.
- **Integrated:** Maintains irregular preterite accuracy alongside regular preterites and present tense. Does not regress on regular forms when producing irregulars.

## Connection Points
This completes the preterite tense. Together with B-01 (regular preterite), the learner now has full access to completed-past narration. B-02 is required for B-04 (preterite vs imperfect), where the challenge shifts from form to meaning. High-frequency irregular preterites (fui, hice, tuve, estuve, dijo, pudo) appear so often that they tend to be acquired faster than some regular forms through sheer repetition. Teach by frequency, not alphabet -- ir/ser, hacer, tener, estar should be automatic before moving to lower-frequency irregulars like andar, producir, or haber.
